messages:
maya.k: Hey team, customer reported embedding vectors coming back with length 768 but their downstream expects 1536. They integrate via our Go SDK and started seeing occasional 429s and then timeout retries that duplicate items. Ticket #C-7392.

maya.k: Minimal repro from customer (Go):
```go
ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 5*time.Second)
defer cancel()
resp, err := client.Embeddings(ctx, embeddings.Payload{Model: "text-embed-2-large", Input: []string{...}})
```
They say SDK v0.9.1.

alex.p: Thanks, tagging eng-ml. Quick Q: are they pinning model in route or using a catalog alias? 768 vs 1536 suggests a small model variant being routed. Any request logs or model field from responses?

maya.k: Customer pasted response fragment: `{"model":"text-embed-1-small", "data": [... vector length 768 ...]}` so looks like routing returned the small model unexpectedly. They claim they set model to text-embed-2-large in code.

samir.r: Two likely causes: 1) routing fallback to a cheaper model when capacity is constrained, 2) local SDK bug modifying the model field when batching/multiplexing. Can you share exact request headers and any retry behavior?

maya.k: They show retries enabled with exponential backoff but using idempotency key only on per-batch basis (so duplicates across retries). Headers: `X-Redwood-Client: embeds-go/0.9.1`, `Retry-After` sometimes present.

ops-bot: [automated] route-fallback-event for customer C-7392: fallback applied to route 'default-embeds' at 2028-11-23T15:12:31Z due to capacity pressure. Fallback target: text-embed-1-small.

irene: That confirms it — fallback happened. Two action items: (A) we should tell customer how to opt out of fallbacks (pin model) or set strict routing policy; (B) investigate why their SDK call had model set to text-embed-2-large but response reports small model (possibly fallback or proxy rewriting).

alex.p: For immediate mitigation: ask them to set model pin in their request: `model: "text-embed-2-large", policy: {allow_fallback: false}` (example payload). Also increase context timeout to 20s to avoid client-side cancels during transient capacity spikes.

maya.k: Provided customer steps and a small ts/py/go snippet for pinning and longer timeout. They tried pinning and got consistent 1536 vectors, but then hit 504s when batch size > 64.

samir.r: 504 + large batch => likely server-side batching limits or request body streaming timeout. Suggest lowering batch size to 32 or enable auto-batching that respects token/size limits. Also check sdk's internal chunking; older Go SDK had a bug where it concatenated batches incorrectly causing malformed inputs and silent fallback. Which commit are they on?

maya.k: They are on tag v0.9.1 (released Aug 2028).

samir.r: Known issue in v0.9.1: when BatchInputs() is used with concurrent calls, a race could merge batch metadata causing model field to be overwritten. Fix shipped in v0.9.2. Recommend upgrade. Quick repro: run concurrent goroutines that call Embeddings with different model strings; inspect outgoing JSON.

alex.p: For retries: recommend setting idempotency on per-item level when possible, or using a unique request id per logical unit to avoid duplicate inserts downstream. Also set Retry-After handling: if response includes `Retry-After`, respect it instead of immediate retry.

maya.k: Customer upgraded to v0.9.2, pinned model, reduced batch to 32, increased timeout to 20s. Outcome: no more 768 vectors, throughput stable, a few 429s but handled by backoff. They still saw occasional long tail latencies at peak.

irene: Follow-up: ask customer to share traces for one problematic request so SRE can correlate server-side queueing. Also propose adding proactive alerting: if route fallback rate > 1% in 5m window, notify owners.

samir.r: I'm creating a small internal runbook for support: steps to triage embedding dimension issues: 1) confirm model in response, 2) check route fallback events, 3) check SDK version for known batching/race bugs, 4) repro locally with pinned model and single worker, 5) advise batch sizing and timeouts, 6) ensure idempotency keys. Will add snippet examples.

maya.k: Customer happy and will schedule dedicated capacity trial. They asked for a short explanation they can share with infra team; I prepared this summary to send.

alex.p: Nice. Also adding a note to release notes about v0.9.2 fix and guidance on `allow_fallback` flag.

maya.k: Closing loop here. Thanks everyone. :tada:
